title: appsec-compose findings.json
description: Consolidated, de-duplicated findings of one appsec-compose run. `schema_version` follows major.minor: the major changes only when a field is removed, renamed or changes meaning; additions bump the minor, so consumers must ignore fields they do not know.

engines.description: Engine -> resolved image ref (a digest when pinned).

databases.description: Vulnerability database -> date it was built.

repo_config.description: 1.4: the scanned repository's own config, when one applied: the keys it set and the ones refused (only project policy is honoured from a repo).

checkov_frameworks.description: 1.3: the Checkov frameworks run — the ones the repository has files for, "all", or "none" (no IaC, Checkov not started).

timings.description: 1.3: where the run's time went. Engines run in parallel, so the scan takes as long as the slowest.

engines.description: Engine -> seconds it ran, slowest first (from Docker's start/finish times).

scanners_s.description: Wall clock of the parallel scanner phase.

collector_s.description: Time the collector took to merge, gate and write reports.

total_s.description: From run.sh start to the reports being written.

min_confidence.description: 1.5: findings from rules that state a lower confidence are reported but do not gate; "low" gates on everything.

fixed.description: Null in diff mode: a baseline entry outside the changed files was not looked for.

legacy_format.description: True when matched against a v1 (line-number) baseline.

fixed_findings.description: 1.6: the baseline's findings not seen in this run, as the baseline recorded them, worst first. Null in diff mode and for a baseline saved before 1.6 (it recorded fingerprints only; re-snapshot with --update-baseline).

licenses.description: Dependency license policy, when `licenses:` is configured (added in 1.1). Denied and warned packages are SCA findings with rule_id LICENSE:<license>.

unlicensed.description: Packages whose manifest records no license, so the policy could not judge them.

metrics.description: 1.5: what the run did, in numbers: time, reports, how the findings were reduced, the size of review-brief.md and the age of the databases. Counts only, never content.

suppressed_in_source.description: suppressed by comments in the code; never part of raw or unique

placeholders.description: secret findings whose value is a placeholder (one repeated character, `your_api_key`, ...); moved to `suppressed` with that reason

brief.description: review-brief.md: its size, and how many findings it shows with code, on one line each (further matches of a rule already shown; low-confidence rules that do not gate) or only counts.

components.description: 1.2: SCA findings grouped by package. A view over `findings`: each finding is still gated, suppressed and baselined on its own.

package.description: name@version, as the engines name it.

upgrade_to.description: Lowest version that fixes every listed vulnerability: per vulnerability the lowest named fix above the installed version, then the highest of those. Plain numeric versions only; null when it cannot be derived.

fixed_in.description: Every fix version an engine names, first seen first; no single upgrade target is computed.

unfixed.description: Vulnerabilities with no known fixed version.

findings.description: Fingerprints of the findings in this component.

scope.description: Since 1.1. What was scanned. `full`: the whole target. `diff` (run.sh --diff): only the files changed between merge-base(base, HEAD) and the working tree, including uncommitted and untracked ones; findings are reported and gated for those files only.

history_scanned.description: Whether those commits were searched for secrets.

deleted.description: Changed files deleted, so not scanned.

skipped_engines.description: Engine -> why it was not run (nothing it reads was changed).

skipped_reports.description: Native report -> why it was not produced; not counted as missing.

out_of_scope_dropped.description: Raw findings outside the changed files, dropped.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity across runs: anchored on the flagged code, not its line number. Usable as an `ignore` selector.

tool.description: Engine whose report represents the merged finding.

rule_id.description: A CVE id when one is known, else the engine's rule id.

severity_stated.description: True when an engine stated the severity; false when derived from CVSS or the SARIF level.

scanner_severity.description: The engines' severity before it was raised (malicious package) or replaced (CVE-PaaS reprioritization), if either happened.

confidence.description: 1.5: how sure the rule is that a match is a real issue, as the engine states it (Semgrep's rule metadata, zizmor per result); "" when it states none. A merged finding takes its surest engine's, or "" when any engine states none.

malicious.description: SCA: the advisory says the package itself is malware (an OpenSSF MAL- id, CWE-506 or a GitHub malware advisory). Always severity critical. Added in 1.1.

file.description: Repo-relative path (an OS path in image mode).

fixed_version.description: SCA: version(s) that fix it, as the engine reported them; empty when none is known.

on_changed_line.description: Since 1.1. Present only in diff mode: true when the finding's span touches a line the change added or modified (every line of a new file); null when there is no line to compare (a dependency, or a secret found only in the branch's commits).
